programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: Queen Elizabeth I goes online dating, Greek philosopher Socrates foils his own rescue from prison, and Emicho of the Rhineland goes crusading with some very unusual satnavs to lead the way.

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: Savage Songs compilation. Featuring the hip-hop battle of the boasting Celts, pop superstar Cleopatra, rock rebel William Wallace, the soulful Suffragettes, the funky Aztec priests, the crooning caveman, bad boy heartthrob Dick Turpin, pouting Richard III, the children of the Victorian workhouses, and the many, many merry monarchs!

programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: Nick and the team travel to Kidderminster to help a family whose lives revolve around caring for their son Nathan. The 11-year-old can have up to 200 seizures a day and needs round-the-clock care, leaving parents John and Emma exhausted. Meanwhile, teenage sister Kira has seen more and more of her home taken over by Nathan's needs. With the help of hundreds of volunteers, the team creates a home that keeps Nathan safe while giving the whole family the space to live together again.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: In 2021, 19-year-old soldier Jaysley Beck was found dead in her army barracks. Through unprecedented access to her family, friends and former colleagues, Stacey Dooley traces her journey from excited young recruit to victim of sexual assault. As her family seeks answers and fights for change, the film explores the experiences of women in the armed forces and asks what more can be done to protect them.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die. As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated. Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death. Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales. Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Rehab centres are treating some of their youngest-ever and most physically damaged addicts, and ketamine has been their drug of choice. Stacey Dooley gains rare access to a rehab in Stockport and gets to know former users. Many are in chronic pain, and one young man needs bladder reconstruction surgery. Over four months, she follows them through recovery, relationships, setbacks and celebrations.

programme.title: The Beasts
programme.desc: Middle-aged French couple Antoine and Olga have moved to an inland Galician hamlet, happy to live off the land and renovate some dilapidated properties, and intending to settle down, but a conflict with their neighbours reaches the point of no return. In French and Spanish with English subtitles

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: On the Northumberland coast, a 999 call comes in from a distressed woman whose husband is drifting out to sea on a paddleboard; the Seahouses crew race out to locate him. In Moelfre, north Wales, when a crew member at the station spots a kayak capsizing, the lifeboat launches to pluck the fishermen from the water. Out in the English Channel, a French vessel makes a distress call, alerting the Torbay crew. And in Calshot, Hampshire, a sailing sloop has become stuck on one of the area’s notorious mudbanks - and is now taking on water.

programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: In Southampton, the team comes to the aid of Ahmed and Rifat, a profoundly deaf couple whose dream home became a nightmare after a rogue builder abandoned the project. With three young children, no savings left and living on a building site, they need help to complete their home and make it work for their family's needs. Nick and the team call on the local community to transform both the house and the family's future.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden continues her airborne exploration of Britain's gardens by dropping in on the county of Essex. At the Beth Chatto Gardens, Christine experiments with triangular planting and shares tea and cake with a gardening legend. At RHS Hyde Hall, she shifts rocks with a former student, and it's all aboard a vintage Thames sailing barge for a trip on the Blackwater Estuary.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: How do you protect Britain’s busiest mountain when more than 600,000 people visit each year? Charlotte Smith and Joe Crowley head to Yr Wyddfa, Wales’s highest peak, to meet the people caring for its landscape and keeping visitors on the move. Joe joins volunteers tackling litter in some of the mountain’s hardest-to-reach gullies before discovering work to protect rare alpine plants and the elusive Snowdon beetle, found nowhere else in the UK. Meanwhile, Charlotte goes behind the scenes at Wales’s highest cafe to find out what it takes to keep visitors fed and watered at the summit. And Tom Heap investigates how organised crime gangs are targeting the countryside.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie heads west to the Morvern Peninsula in Lochaber to find out how Ardtornish Estate is being run to balance farming and stalking with nature restoration. Anne is on a photoshoot in Glenshee with a portrait photographer using Scotland’s landscape as her backdrop, and Leanna is near Kingussie encountering some misunderstood blood-sucking creatures that are being saved from extinction. Rosie visits the dairy farm near Peterhead that diversified and created new markets for their milk, and Dougie steps out with a herd of rare Irish cattle.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek gets some northern nostalgia as he remembers three of his best walks in north Wales. Cadair Idris is a mountain steeped in legend and mythology - it's also one of Wales's most spectacular summits. Derek climbs to three peaks in this range and even braves an icy cold dip in its glacial lake, where the temperature, quite literally, takes his breath away. The second walk Derek recalls is from the Italianate village of Portmeirion, where he also discovers Y Gwyllt - ‘the wild’ headland beyond. Finally, Derek walks the Dee Valley Way, a stunning 13-mile route which takes him from the pretty town of Corwen to its larger and more bustling neighbour, Llangollen. On the walk, he learns of a warrior prince and leads a horse-drawn barge along the Llangollen canal.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt brings an abundance of autumnal flavours to the table with help from some Saturday Kitchen chefs. Bryn Williams celebrates the best of the season's produce with a delicious butternut squash and chestnut tart, served with a winter salad and crispy deep-fried sage leaves. Selin Kaizim brings a taste of Cyprus to the studio with her beef and bulgur wheat koftes, while David Carter makes aubergines the stars of the show. Julie Lin makes a dish packed with crispy fried fish, cucumber, melted cheese, a punchy sambal and a side of crinkle-cut fries. Poppy O’Toole adds spices and harissa to a classic cottage pie base before topping with a fresh chilli and herb mash. And Bryan Cranston and Marianne Jean-Baptiste battle it out for their food heaven. Meanwhile, Rick Stein sets out to prove that old-fashioned veg is best, and the Hairy Bikers learn the history behind one of the world’s most famous condiments in Menorca.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Eva and her Breton guide Tanguy Thomassin explore the vast oyster beds of Cancale, oyster capital of Brittany. Being pummelled by one of the highest tides in Europe makes for fatter, sweeter and healthier oysters. And having once supplied King Louis XVI’s oyster habit, Brittany still supplies half of France. Bretons also boast of plentiful sardines, kelp forests, spiny crabs and the rare cobalt blue lobster. Fished sustainably and cooked on a grill, it's little wonder that this beauty is called the king of lobsters.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Multimillionaire landowner Paul Lister wants to turn his 23,000-acre estate north of Inverness into Europe's first wilderness reserve. Reinstating the old Caledonian pine forests is the first of his plans. He then wants to release long-lost animals, starting with moose and wild boar, and eventually predators such as brown bears, lynx and wolves. Some of the local people are far from convinced by Paul's vision. Will he even be allowed to let loose moose in the glen?

programme.title: Gymnastics World Championships
programme.desc: Coverage of the second part of the apparatus finals from Rotterdam, the Netherlands, featuring the men's vault, parallel bars and horizontal bars, and the women's balance beam and floor.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The team are in Gloucester, where presenter Paul Martin and experts Phillip Serrell and Michael Baggott discover some rare gems among the antiques and collectibles brought to the valuation day at the city's magnificent cathedral.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: From the road trip back catalogue, three of Tim Medhurst's favourite pop stars try their hand at our antiques-buying challenge. Vying to be top of the pops are 90s heartthrob Peter Andre, the golden boy of the new romantics, Spandau Ballet's Martin Kemp, and an 80s pop icon, the mega-glamorous Sinitta. They are guided along the way by experts Paul Laidlaw, Margie Cooper, and the 'so macho' Tim Medhurst, helping them to hunt down timeless treasures. Sinitta lights up the saleroom with some illuminating items, Martin goes radio gaga, and Peter takes a punt on part of a plane!

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve travels across Mongolia – the most sparsely populated country on Earth and home to some of the most brutal and beautiful landscapes on the planet. Six times the size of the UK but with fewer than 3.5 million people, Simon wants to find out how nomadic traditions, such as hunting with golden eagles, and wild nature still shape everyday life, all while searching for the elusive snow leopard.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Sitting between Germany and France, Alsace is frontier land with a cuisine to match. In Strasbourg, Eva stops off at Brasserie Le Tigre for a beer (brassier means ‘to brew’) and a deliciously creamy tarte flambee. Then there's a trip to guide Coralie Andt’s restaurant, known as a winstub, where French wines can be enjoyed with plenty of cheese and sausage – as well as more sausage with sauerkraut cooked in white Riesling wine. With French tarts in a brasserie that serves German-style beer, and German sausage in a winstub serving French white wine, Alsace is defined by its competing national influences.

programme.title: The Balkans: Europe’s Forgotten Frontier
programme.desc: Katya Adler travels to Romania, Kosovo and Serbia. In Romania, Katya visits what will soon be Nato’s largest base in Europe. With Russia’s increasing aggression, Nato’s role in eastern Europe has been beefed up, and Romania has become strategically significant. Katya’s next stop is Europe’s youngest country, Kosovo. She travels down Tony Blair Street – named after the UK prime minister who led the Nato mission there. Twenty-five years after the war ended, Katya meets the ethnic Serbs who still live in Kosovo – and insist the country is still Serbian. Lastly, in Serbia, she visits a coal power plant and discovers there’s a battle for power taking place, with the west, Russia and China all wanting Serbia to be in their sphere of influence. For decades, the west has ignored this corner of Europe, but now, with so many other parts of the world gaining power and influence, the fear is Europe might be losing its foothold in this increasingly important region.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob travel to the River Ribble in Lancashire for one last fish with their little canine pal, Ted. The beautiful river Ribble runs through the rolling hills of the Yorkshire Dales, onwards to Lancashire before meeting the Irish Sea in Lytham. With the river in good health, Paul and Bob hope to catch a good chub or a mighty barbel on this stretch of the water, while Ted hopes to taste Bob’s Lancashire hotpot.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Hollywood legend Bill Murray begins a journey around Ireland, combining golf with a search for his Irish roots. But travelling with Bill rarely goes to plan. In Kinsale, chance encounters turn a simple walk into an adventure, while friend and golf writer Tom Coyne tries to keep things on track. Golf brought Bill to Ireland, but the best moments often happen far from the course.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools welcomes Dexys Midnight Runners, Courtney Barnett, Madra Salach, Ibibio Sound Machine, Mulaa Joans and Elkie Brooks to the show.

programme.title: Misery
programme.desc: Author Paul Sheldon is injured in a car accident on a remote snowy road. He is saved by nurse Annie Wilkes, a great fan of his work, but her devotion soon takes a sinister turn.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Is the UK already fighting in a proxy World War? Fiona Bruce presents topical debate from Scunthorpe, featuring defence secretary Wes Streeting for Labour, shadow foreign secretary Tom Tugendhat for the Conservatives, the Greens’ Ellie Chowns, journalist and economist Stephanie Flanders and comedian and radio host Geoff Norcott. With defence spending expected to be increased in next week’s Budget, watch what the Question Time panel from Scunthorpe said on hybrid 'grey zone' warfare and threats from Russia, as well as new gas drilling in the North Sea, the state of the NHS and re-industrialising the UK.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: Lee is sceptical about all the witchy woo-woo stuff on display at an alternative craft fair where Lucy is trying to sell her badly made dream catchers. Unfortunately, his attitude irritates everyone there and ensures that Lucy can’t sell any of her stock.

programme.title: Ellie & Natasia
programme.desc: Ellie White and Natasia Demetriou make a chaotic return to the screen, reuniting with some of the show's most iconic creations - including a deeply passionate food review centred on bread, internet entrepreneurs Donna and Nikki trying to scale their beauty empire to dizzying new heights, and a duo of digital creators whose egos are only outsized by their wardrobe. Plus a guest appearance by Steve Coogan.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Two parent-and-daughter duos dash with their cash around a bustling antiques fair in Kent, searching for collectibles to sell at auction.

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Hugh meets designers Robin and Eoin on their journey to convert a Victorian schoolhouse into a chic family home. However, after delays and setbacks, can they transform this functional space into the home of their dreams? Presented by Hugh Wallace.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: A busy Premier League Sunday, with five matches, including Liverpool against a Brighton side who’ve started the season strongly, and Manchester United at home to struggling Bournemouth. Elsewhere, Brentford, another side who have enjoyed early-season form, travel to Hull City, two of last season’s promoted clubs Sunderland and Leeds United meet at the Stadium of Light, and Pierre Sage’s Crystal Palace take on Newcastle United.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Edith Bowman and Colin Murray explore the Stranraer Oyster Festival, sailing into Loch Ryan to Scotland’s largest wild oyster bed to discover why they’re so special. Baker Briony-May Williams reveals the effort behind every bag of frozen peas, and farmer Meinir Howells goes underground to find the secret of cheesemaking in Harlech. Ryan Hand is in Armagh on the hunt for a healthy ready meal.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo embarks on a journey across Essex. Beginning on the fringes of London, he takes the underground to the ancient woodland of Epping Forest, with its gnarled hornbeams and beeches, a legacy of centuries of pollarding. Continuing on the Central Line, Michael visits a historic London Transport signal cabin in Epping which has been preserved by railway enthusiasts. He guides an underground train into Epping station – on a simulator. At Harlow, Michael visits the house and garden of the town’s chief architect, Sir Frederick Gibberd. Michael hears about Gibberd’s plan for Harlow's new town and discovers the architect’s love of art and sculpture in the garden. At Audley End, he visits a charming miniature railway which has recently celebrated its 60th anniversary and learns of Audley End House's role as a secret wartime military school.

programme.title: Earth’s Tropical Islands
programme.desc: Journey across Madagascar, the oldest island on earth. Over time, it has given rise to more unique plants and animals, from its lemurs to chameleons, than any other island.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Wilton House near Salisbury where a rich hoard of treasures and curiosities are brought to light. Included in the day's finds are a hoard of 200 typewriters, a suffragette doll dressed in clothes cut from women protestors' prison uniforms, a ring once worn by the daughter of Charles I, and an ornate table, transported in the back of a horsebox.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes to Blackburn in Lancashire, where the valuation day is being held at Blackburn Cathedral. The experts are Charles Hanson and Anita Manning. Anita discovers an Omar Ramsden spoon, and Charles finds an old silver bucket that has been used as a bin and a Christmas tree holder but turns out to be Faberge! Paul Martin learns about how mill workers in Blackburn during the industrial revolution were woken by a human alarm clock known as ‘a knocker upper’.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Les Dennis, Jenny Eclair, Owain Wyn Evans and Lauren Patel take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor kicks off the week by chatting to the latest couple to be eliminated from the competition, and Friday’s all-star panel return to break down all the ballroom action from the weekend.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Nawal Al-Maghafi reports from Yemen's front lines, where Houthi forces are posing the most serious threat in years to the city of Taiz, raising fears of a major escalation in a conflict that has endured for more than a decade. We also trace the roots of Yemen's war, exploring how the country's strategic location has drawn it into a struggle involving Saudi Arabia, Iran and the United States. Plus: BBC Mundo travels to Panama's Coiba Island, a biodiversity hotspot, to explore how a former prison colony helped preserve a rare and fragile natural world.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The series continues with another four contenders facing the black chair, answering questions on their chosen specialist subjects to earn a place in the semi-finals. Clive Myrie hosts, and the subjects are the record label Creation Records, The X-Files, the 1815 Waterloo military campaign and the Hollywood actress Gene Tierney.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Neither team is leaving the tournament this time, but the questions are as challenging as ever. What connects the following: impossible question, unexpectedly blue, safe woods and uninformed loop?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: In the second of the round one repechage games, Bristol and Queen’s University Belfast compete for the final place in the second round. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc: In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president - a former boxer and soldier - as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda. But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British - with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime. With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports?

programme.title: QI
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig takes tea with Rosie Jones, Ahir Shah, Henning Wehn and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Eye Investigations

programme.desc: Preston’s automated scooter tour of Swoppiton doesn’t go as planned. Mojo and Bo must find a way to chase down and scoop up those scooters, and get the tour back on track!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Norrie skips into the Clubhouse and greets her friends. Together, they reflect on their first meeting. Arriving with her parents in a long limousine, Norrie, her parents and her 72 siblings flood out of the car. It's just Norrie who is going to stay at the Clubhouse, though, and enjoy some well-needed quiet. She can play alone and hear herself think! But after a while, she misses the hustle and bustle, so Duggee introduces Norrie to Enid the cat. Together, they venture into the Clubhouse, and Norrie has a friend so she isn't alone, but she still has a little bit more room than she would have at home!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Snail is thrilled to be moving house as she wishes to escape the wet and sploshy place she currently calls home for a more spacious house on the hill. But before she can move up in the world, she’s going to need some help from Duggee and the Squirrels to move her many belongings up the hill! Snail can’t do it alone, so Duggee teaches the Squirrels the best ways that they can get moving! They band together, cradling items and shifting furniture. Snail looks on with apprehension as they manage fragile vases with less care than she’d like. Luckily, Duggee intercepts the vases before they crash head first into one another and teaches the Squirrels all the ways they can move to ensure Snail has a stress-free and efficient move. They could lift, push or pull to get things moving! They work together as a team to get the job done before Snail can even reach the house, so they give her a helping hand too.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey wants to know why Dad is always bossing her around!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: At school, Bluey and her friends turn a tree stump into a thrilling helicopter game. But as the pilot, Bluey has to learn to give up some control so they can all have fun.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: While shopping in Istanbul's Grand Bazaar, Glitch wishes he could have some of everything. Hearing about the wishes granted by the Hen's Eye Column in an underground water store, the Basilica Cistern, Glitch heads beneath the earth. But when he gets his thumb stuck inside the column, he ends up bringing the entire cistern close to collapse! Will Foz be able to save the ancient structure without the help of click-ons?

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Cheeky Peter Rabbit loves adventure but he struggles to stay out of trouble. Luckily his best friends are always around to help him out. Based on Beatrix Potter's classic stories.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: The Octonauts guide migrating monarch butterflies on a journey south for the winter.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The Rainbow Sevens have gathered to make one big Rainbow Seven mural. Numberblock Sixty-three meets each friend that makes up the Rainbow Sevens to see what they have planned for their paintings, and to get inspiration for his own painting too. Each of the Rainbow Sevens have their own rainbow styles, underneath one great big, colourful rainbow.

programme.title: Wonderblocks
programme.desc: The Three Bears are struggling to make their breakfast in the right order because they all want to go first! Go, Stop and the Breakfast Crew help them figure things out.

programme.title: Love Monster
programme.desc: Love Monster is finding it hard to think of something new to do on Do Something New Day, so he heads to Tiniest Fluffiest Bunny’s house to see if she has any ideas.

programme.title: Justin's House
programme.desc: It’s time to have a picnic for teddy bears in the Justin’s House garden! Robert has been looking after all the arrangements, and Little Monster and Justin have brought their teddies with them to enjoy the fun. Robert calls the Justin Times to ask them to put out an advert. He is inviting the whole of Justin Town to come to their special picnic for bears. Soon the doorbell rings, and Robert is surprised to find two full-sized bears there. He realises he said it was a picnic for bears and not teddy bears!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Sula’s cousin Nicky is visiting, something Bing is a little unsure about. Sula and Bing start making 'rippy pictures', and while Sula is looking for some purple paper Bing shows Nicky how to voosh the blue speedy car down the slide. However, Nicky vooshes too, falling and breaking his glasses! Sula is furious and Bing is forlorn. Amma soothes Bing while Nicky shows him that he can click his glasses back together again.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘nose’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see lots of different noses – long noses, little noses, blowing noses and snoring noses. We see twitchy noses on bunnies, sniffy noses on dogs, funny noses and even someone dressed as a nose! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Tralala
programme.desc: When Tralala finds her rhythm, Batty searches for hers too. Can they share?

programme.title: MaeBee
programme.desc: Trying to cure Ma-Mae’s anger while painting a moving mural, Mae and Bee ask Witch Linda for a happy spell. Instead, she sends them on an even more infuriating quest!

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri and Lou meet a shy little creature called Small. It turns out she’s a fan, and she’s even written a song about them!

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a living room, where they see a man going outside into the garden through the patio doors. He brings some things outside with him, a chair and then a cushion, and finally a book which he starts to read. The Twirlywoos decide to move more things from inside the house to the outside, while the man obliviously continues reading. They get carried away, and when the man finally looks up from his book, he finds he is surrounded by the entire contents of the living room, even the sofa! Peekaboo gets stuck outside the boat and goes around it looking in through different windows and making noises which the Twirlywoos hear, but can't see who it is. Finally, Peekaboo manages to get back inside through the top of the boat.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Today, Justin and his friend are animal keepers at an animal park. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble is caring for an animal too.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The voice trumpet leads a game of I Spy where the Teletubbies have to spot different colours - purple, green, yellow and red. What or who can they spot with those colours?

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Marta, Billie, Hud, Elijah, Thomas, Finley and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside Giovanna’s bag is a rubber duck, and all the parents and babies have different bath toys in their bags which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding a baby appropriate rubber duck or bath toy inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The nursery rhyme Three Little Ducks features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Together Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: I Spy, You Spy
programme.desc: Elsee plays I-spy in a garden centre with her new friend Karlie.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie is at home waiting for the postman. She’s expecting a letter from Uncle George, everybody’s favourite uncle, but each time she hears a knock at the door, it seems to be someone else! Maybe today’s not the day for George’s letter?

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: No, Rebecca isn’t wearing a box on her head - she’s dressed as an astronaut! This gives Murphi an idea. He helps Rebecca discover alien life by creating an alien out of a sock. The Mini Monsters are making skyscapes, Rebecca’s royal relative is looking for something, and the final mega monster make is another space-inspired creation. The Recycling Express and the Tiny Helpers support Rebecca and Murphi as they reach for the stars.

programme.title: Raa Raa the Noisy Lion
programme.desc: Topsy has readied the musical stones for a noisy game. Raa Raa has been left in charge, making sure that nobody jumps on them while Topsy reminds the other jungle inhabitants about the game. But temptation can be strong, especially when Ooo Ooo is about...

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey is running a taxi service. Her first passenger is Businessman Dad, who is in a rush to get to the airport. But with unexpected delays, Dad's in danger of missing his flight!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Betty is reading a story out loud to the other Squirrels that is set 'a long, long time ago'. The Squirrels wonder how long ago that is. The narrator explains that it's everything that's ever happened – and it's called history. The Squirrels are excited to learn about it, and luckily Duggee has his History Badge – and a home-made time machine - to give them a very interactive lesson all about it! The Squirrels go on a whistle-stop tour through time and encounter all manner of characters, from naughty prehistoric monkeys to pirates of the high seas, from Isaac Newton to Shakespeare, with everyone becoming inspired as they go. History is FUN - but eventually it's time to go home and collect their History Badges. Well done Squirrels!

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Elena finds out all about marvellous moths. Chantelle is with Dr Amir Khan to see one of the world’s biggest moths while Rory and his son Sandy are in disguise being moth spies. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain how moths hide, how they can find their way in the dark and the differences between moths and butterflies. It’s also time to find out how moths help the planet at night. This episode’s Teeny Tiny Task is to plant some night-flowering plants.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Audrey and her family visit a farm. They meet some of the animals up close, and Audrey feeds the guinea pigs with a carrot treat before enjoying cuddles with a baby goat. Then it’s off for a tractor ride, where Audrey meets a horse with a moustache!

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Jen has brought in the board game snakes and ladders but has lost the dice. Camar the crocodile comes to visit, Small whizzes off to see how courgettes grow, and the two chefs make courgette crocodile for their snappy guest.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Guide dog Kika and her owner Dr Amit are off to the Sticks 'n’ Stuff shop with Amit’s friend Alana, who is also blind, to help her buy a new white cane.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a vulture called Ethel. Vultures have amazing eyesight and can spot food from high up in the sky. To meet their next animal, Aneeshwar and Lizzie must go far down below. The brittlestar lives underwater in the ocean. This incredible creature has five long arms and a body called a disc. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: What’s in Your Bag?
programme.desc: In this episode, we meet Ajmal, an Imam who tells us all about how his Rehal helps to hold important books and why it’s so important to him as a Muslim.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba can't wait for his swimming lesson, and he has a great instructor - his big sister. Oona teaches Baba to paddle, steer with his feet and put his head under the water. With some practice and encouragement from Oona and Mama, Baba starts to get the hang of it - but diving proves much more difficult, until Lala drops a shiny shell in the water.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: When Yukee is asked to carry several messages across the garden to Sonny, she comes up with a clever rhyming song to help her remember them all.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Biba gets frustrated when Lu abandons their cushion castle to play with baby Bo.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Fred and Dana ask the Piggies to plan fun outdoor games for Keith and Rebecca. Each piggy comes up with an idea, but Cesar’s is so ambitious that he can’t tackle it alone!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Numberland is rocked by the arrival of superblock Eight, known to his friends and fans as Octoblock. Learn all about the number 8 with Numberblock Eight!

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: O is fascinated as G grows her green hair into a grassy garden. P and friends pop in to make a popping pea pod in a pot, but when a digging dog shows up, it is time for trouble. This episode introduces the letters G and O and the words pot, pod, dog and dig.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: It’s a hot day, so Justin and his friends cool off by visiting an ice cream farm. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble tries to keep Spotty cool but can’t seem to control his hosepipe!

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Preschool series. It's time to wake up, but Tinky Winky isn't feeling well. Soon after, Tinky Winky feels better, but now Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po don't feel well.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Baby rhino Malaika tries something new to eat. Hamza spots some huge hippos in the wild and helps the baby zebras at the orphanage stay cosy with some warm blankets.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Maddie is making breakfast in the kitchen. She visits a farm to see where eggs come from and uses a special thermal imaging camera to show why eggs change colour when they're cooked. Next, Maddie visits a mill to see how kernels of wheat are ground and turned into flour. She then visits a factory to find out how the flour is made into different types of bread and baked in a very large oven.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this fast and exciting episode, CBeebies' very own motorbike rider Grace shows off three amazing machines that are all designed to race! Grace drives a rally car in the forest, shows off some incredible racing trucks and then has an actual race in a Stoxkart!

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: It’s Silas and his classmates' first full day at school! There are lots of things to explore, new friends to make and teachers to meet. After meeting the teachers, the children explore the classroom and outdoor area. At lunchtime, Ottilie and Bryn ‘spot’ an invisible mouse in the dining hall. Lusungu finds that opening yogurt lids can be a bit tricky. Luckily, Mrs Farrell is on hand to help. The day continues as Silas and Maily create family portraits. Silas has fun drawing his mum's, but finds it harder to draw his pet cats - so he draws rabbits instead!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Scoops and cones at the ready as Iona and Elba make some tasty ice creams!

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger can't get a wink of sleep when the baby Pea-Rexes start snoring loudly.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. While Kwazii and Peso have their hands full babysitting a bunch of Adelie penguin chicks, Captain Barnacles must rescue the chicks' parents from a perilous sea storm!

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Sammy Whiskers and Tommy Brock steal the rabbits' go-kart - with Cotton-tail on board - Peter needs to race faster than ever to rescue his sister!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Bing Bong! There's somebody at the door. It's Delivery Chipmunk with a parcel for Duggee, but why is it wrapped up like a present? Maybe it's Duggee's birthday! The Squirrels decide they should have a party, but they will have to keep it a secret as it's a very BIG surprise.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Out in the ocean, the Piripenguins encounter a massive, angry whale called Norman, who wrecks their boat. Can the Piripenguins brave their fears and find a way to cheer him up?

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato and Evil Pea get stuck inside a giant bubble together. They float through the air until Supertato and Evil Pea pop the bubble by driving it into a supermarket sign.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Weasy and the Ducklings discover a treasure map. Weasy steals it and sets off alone on the trail, but the Ducklings are determined not to miss out and want the map back!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Ted the bus wants to be faster, and Mojo swops every top to try to make it happen. But it’s Bo’s homemade rocket that gives Ted the boost he needs... all the way into space!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey wants to know why Dad is always bossing her around!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: At school, Bluey and her friends turn a tree stump into a thrilling helicopter game. But as the pilot, Bluey has to learn to give up some control so they can all have fun.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Spark isn’t feeling well, but Madam Dragon insists he is fine - just over-excited for his lesson. Zog’s intuition tells him Madam Dragon is wrong, but can he tell her?

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: When Ava’s dad can’t lead the Balamory Games, she searches for a new chieftain. But then Dynamite the Gladiator surprises her by placing the chieftain’s hat upon Ava’s head.

programme.title: Waffle's After School Club
programme.desc: Mrs Hobbs challenges the after schoolers to vote for their favourite activity - and to do it again on Mr Brooklyn-Bell's arrival.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wishes for a brave dragon to protect her from a storm but finds a scared one instead. She discovers how to help somebody else face their fears.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo thinks she’s seen every animal that visits Cynthia’s garden. But Cynthia shows JoJo her new night-time camera, which can take photos of nocturnal animals JoJo has never seen. Gran Gran has a plan to help JoJo discover these night-time animals – they can leave a footprint tracker out overnight outside her house to find out which ones visit them. The next day, they check the tracker. As hoped, there are lots of prints: hedgehogs, foxes and more! Best of all, Cynthia gets some photographs of the night-time animals to share too.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Sarah is a seven-year-old girl with big eyes and a green hat, who lives with her quacky, flappy, slightly manic but endearing best friend Duck. The pair embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. On a windy day, Sarah and Duck try to get their new kite to fly.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Small is unhappy with his drawing, so he finds a place to practise in peace. Major Clanger discovers some wonderful wall pictures in an underground cave and invites everyone to see them, but it turns out that Small has seen the pictures before.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo is drawing a picture of BaBa, but BaBa can’t sit still. MeMo paints a picture at the Play Tree, but the Tweeties accidentally step all over it. BaBa loves the messy painting, as do the Yummies. They add their own flourishes, and MeMo starts to see its beauty. Pungi, Fungi and Elewhale also add to the picture. MeMo thinks it is a beautiful painting made by all their friends.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Children's series set in a magical garden. The Tombliboos are in their house when Makka Pakka comes to call. In their haste to leave, Tombliboo Eee keeps going the wrong way. Finally, they discover they can find their way together.

programme.desc: Join Tom Hardy for the story of Milo, a little boy with a big new feeling.

programme.desc: Claina Palmer returns to HobbyMaker with more papercrafting and new creative projects to explore, sharing fresh ideas, step-by-step inspiration, and beautiful makes.
